name: German public works award intelligence
demand: Destatis reports 199,334 public awards worth €135.2bn and 11,524 reporting offices for 2024; these are market-size proxies across all contract types, not counts of likely software buyers. No verified search-volume, install, or user-demand figures found. The official page presents data through 2024: https://www.destatis.de/EN/Themes/Government/Public-Finance/Public-procurement/_node.html
prices: Kontor Data advertises €79/month plus VAT, cancellable monthly, with its price page dated 9 Oct 2026: https://kontordata.com/en/pricing. Alternatives include free official TED/DÖE notices, TendiGo from €32/month with annual billing (https://tendigo.de/preise), VergabeHero from €69/month (https://vergabehero.eu/preise), Patterno from €89/month with annual billing (https://www.patterno.de/de/preise), and a free searchable award directory from Tender Republic (https://ausschreibungen.tenderrepublic.de/). These are advertised prices, not proof of sales.
copy_speed: High for a generic award database: Kontor Data already offers the core company, buyer, award, bid-count and competitor analysis described in this lead (https://kontordata.com/en/pricing; methodology: https://kontordata.com/methodik). Minerva and aufträge.io also describe buyer/supplier profiles and historical winner analysis (https://www.useminerva.com/de/funktionen/marktanalyse; https://www.auftraege.io/facts/); Tender Republic provides a free searchable directory with award winners and values (https://ausschreibungen.tenderrepublic.de/). Since April 2026, VergabeRadar states it was founded 15 July 2026, but its described product is tender matching rather than the same historical analytics (https://www.vergabe-radar.com/ueber-uns); Marketplace D was announced live on 15 Oct 2026, an adjacent procurement marketplace rather than award analytics (https://www.smartcountry.berlin/en/newsblog/details/marketplace-d-is-now-live.html). Exact launch dates for the direct analytics competitors were not verified.
platform_risk: Moderate. TED provides open procurement data for analysis and reuse (https://data.ted.europa.eu/; https://docs.ted.europa.eu/api/latest/search.html). Germany's DÖE provides an Open Data interface, but its own description says EU-wide notices are mandatory there while below-threshold coverage is not established as complete (https://www.bescha.bund.de/DE/ElektronischerEinkauf/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf/Bekanntmachungsservice/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf_node.html). Kontor's methodology likewise says its record history and portal coverage vary by source and that bidder/value fields appear only when published (https://kontordata.com/methodik). Marketplace D may change tender discovery, but it does not presently replace historical award analysis (https://www.smartcountry.berlin/en/newsblog/details/marketplace-d-is-now-live.html).
defensible_asset: A carefully deduplicated, source-linked history with reliable buyer and supplier identity matching could qualify as a compiled-data moat. It is weak as proposed: the underlying TED data is reusable, DÖE exposes open data, and multiple products already sell or publish normalized award and competitor analysis. The lead's stated asset is therefore reproducible unless it develops materially better coverage, identity resolution, or a unique dataset. Sources: https://data.ted.europa.eu/; https://docs.ted.europa.eu/api/latest/search.html; https://kontordata.com/methodik; https://www.useminerva.com/de/funktionen/marktanalyse; https://www.auftraege.io/facts/.
build_effort: High for a reliable nationwide service. A narrow TED/DÖE prototype is feasible, but full source coverage, deduplication, supplier matching, missing-field handling, source-linked corrections, and ongoing monitoring are continuing work. Kontor's published methodology documents multiple source types, entity-matching rules, incomplete fields, and daily recalculation (https://kontordata.com/methodik). A solo build timetable is unverified.
channel: Use indexable buyer/supplier/award pages for SEO, opt-in reports, and contextual paid search; do not use cold messages or calls. UK ICO guidance says PECR's direct-marketing message rules do not apply to online advertising, while cookie and data-protection rules can still apply (https://ico.org.uk/media/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr-2-4.pdf). Germany's UWG treats unsolicited advertising email and certain calls as unacceptable nuisance, so avoid those channels (https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_uwg/englisch_uwg.html).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; no public evidence supports the <=5 h/week constraint. The published source and update requirements imply ongoing exception handling, but the actual workload is unknown (https://kontordata.com/methodik).
automation_reason: Rough estimate for mature recurring operations, not observed performance: ingestion, deduplication, routine classification, alerts, reporting, billing administration, and first-line support are plausible automation targets. Source failures, ambiguous entity matches, data-quality decisions, product direction, and customer acquisition still need human oversight. The documented source variation and matching rules make the >=50% target uncertain (https://kontordata.com/methodik).
moat_assessment: Conditional data moat, but not a defensible gap today. The specific product wedge in the lead already exists at Kontor Data, and competing historical-award and buyer/supplier analytics exist at Minerva and aufträge.io. Free official data and free competitor listings make normalization and trust the paid value; no independent evidence shows this proposed entrant can outperform incumbents on coverage or accuracy. Sources: https://kontordata.com/en/pricing; https://www.useminerva.com/de/funktionen/marktanalyse; https://www.auftraege.io/facts/; https://ausschreibungen.tenderrepublic.de/.
desk_test: One day, no cold outreach: choose one construction trade and region, create a small source-linked sample from official TED/DÖE records, and compare it with the free directory and Kontor results. Publish a clearly labelled preview with the intended price and an opt-in request for a paid pilot; run a small contextual search-ad test. Do not build the full database unless inbound users identify a specific coverage or analysis gap and accept the stated price. Official source access and free rival coverage: https://data.ted.europa.eu/; https://www.bescha.bund.de/DE/ElektronischerEinkauf/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf/Bekanntmachungsservice/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf/Datenservice_Oeffentlicher_Einkauf_node.html; https://ausschreibungen.tenderrepublic.de/.
red_flags: The cheap kill-check's claim that no equivalent cross-buyer competitor analysis was found is contradicted by Kontor Data itself, whose cited pricing page describes the same core product. The €79 price is only an advertised price; no verified transaction, revenue, churn, or customer-payment evidence was found. <=5 owner hours/week is unverified. Recommendation: kill the generic clone; only continue if the one-day test finds and validates a narrow, underserved data wedge. Sources: https://kontordata.com/en/pricing; https://kontordata.com/methodik.
